html:
On 13 May 2005 Uzbek government troops fired on a large crowd of protesters in Andijan, a city in the Fergana Valley of Uzbekistan. The government said 187 people died; witnesses and rights groups said several hundred, and some claimed far more.

The trigger was a trial of 23 local businessmen accused of Islamic extremism. During the night armed men freed them from prison and took over the regional government building. The next day thousands of people gathered on the main square, many to complain about poverty and the government of President Islam Karimov. Troops then fired into the crowd, including people fleeing.

Hundreds fled across the border to Kyrgyzstan. Karimov refused an international inquiry. When the United States and the European Union criticised him, he expelled American forces from their air base in Uzbekistan and turned toward Russia and China. Andijan is also the birthplace of Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire.
